executive_preview: The clearest industry shift this week is not a single product launch but a more pragmatic approach to electrification. GM is reopening the hybrid path while closing or repurposing some EV- and hydrogen-focused facilities; Ford is making the Mach-E more affordable and versatile; and suppliers including Bosch and CATL are maintaining technology optionality across electric, hydrogen and multiple battery chemistries. At the same time, automakers are moving software-defined architectures beyond EVs, with GM targeting centralized computing across gas and electric vehicles.

lead_development.title: Battery and charging strategies are becoming more infrastructure-aware.
lead_development.what_happened: Electrify America opened its largest reported charging station in Orlando; LAZ Parking and EverCharge proposed load-sharing for apartment charging; Honda developed underlying technology for in-motion wireless charging; and Redwood expanded battery recycling with Rivian.
lead_development.why_it_matters: The constraint is increasingly system deployment rather than only vehicle range. Shared electrical capacity, high-throughput sites, recycling and future wireless systems address different parts of the ownership ecosystem.

signals.title: GM Rebalances Its Portfolio Toward Hybrids and Flexible Propulsion
signals.teaser: GM said it plans to add hybrids across multiple segments without additional capital spending or engineering, while its earnings coverage reported the closure of the Brownstown Battery Assembly plant and repurposing of another facility intended for hydrogen fuel-cell development.

signals.title: Software-Defined Vehicle Architecture Is Moving Beyond EVs
signals.teaser: GM announced a centralized compute architecture for autonomous driving, in-car AI, powertrain management and connected services.

signals.title: Autonomy Is Advancing Through Constrained Commercial Deployments

downside.title: Software failures could turn convenience features into mobility, safety or customer-trust problems.
downside.teaser: Reported update behavior temporarily prevented a Hyundai Kona from starting, while a Tesla robotaxi could not disable a novelty audio feature during a customer ride.

upside.title: Use CPO and carefully sourced lower-priced used vehicles to address affordability gaps.
upside.teaser: CPO sales rose 10% year over year, while sub-$15,000 used inventory remained tighter than the overall market.
